research_target: Fused Single-Pass SIMD JSON Parser: Beating simdjson with Speculative Structural Indexing and Zero-Copy On-Demand Parsing
viral_thesis: simdjson parses JSON at gigabytes per second using a two-pass SIMD approach (structural indexing then tape generation). We hypothesize that fusing these passes via speculative execution — borrowing branch prediction concepts from CPU microarchitecture — combined with AVX-512 VBMI2 compress-store instructions and a novel predictive structural classifier, can eliminate the second pass entirely for common JSON shapes, achieving 1.5-3x speedup over simdjson 4.3 on real-world workloads. A JSON parser that verifiably beats the fastest parser in the world would generate massive excitement.

items.description: Design and implement speculative single-pass fused structural indexer + tape generator
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in C (with AVX-512 intrinsics) a novel fused parser that: (1) performs structural character classification AND tape/DOM construction in a single pass over the input, (2) uses speculative execution: predicts likely structure based on preceding context (e.g., after '{' expect string key, after ':' expect value), speculatively writes tape entries, and corrects on misprediction, (3) leverages VPCOMPRESSB (AVX-512 VBMI2) for branchless extraction of structural characters into dense buffers, (4) implements a lightweight finite automaton that validates UTF-8, tracks nesting, and builds the output representation simultaneously, (5) handles the 'easy path' (well-structured, shallow JSON) with zero branches in the hot loop. Code must compile and pass basic correctness tests. Produce src/fused_parser.c and src/fused_parser.h.

items.description: Implement predictive structural classifier using JSON shape statistics
items.acceptance_criteria: Build a prediction module (src/predictor.c, src/predictor.h) that: (1) maintains a small (<=256 byte) prediction state encoding recent structural patterns, (2) predicts the next N structural characters given current context using a precomputed lookup table trained on the JSON statistics from item_011, (3) achieves >85% prediction accuracy on the standard test corpus, (4) prediction check and correction path costs at most 2 extra instructions on the fast path (correct prediction) and at most 15 instructions on the slow path (misprediction), (5) prediction accuracy and overhead measured and documented in results/experiments/predictor_accuracy.json. Concept tree exploration: use concept_evolve 'reframe' on 'branch prediction applied to data parsing' across CPU architecture, compression, and machine learning domains.

items.description: Implement zero-copy arena-based on-demand DOM with SIMD-accelerated string handling
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement output representation (src/arena_dom.c, src/arena_dom.h) that: (1) uses a single contiguous arena allocation (no per-node malloc), (2) strings are represented as (pointer, length) pairs pointing directly into the original input buffer — true zero-copy for unescaped strings, (3) escaped strings are lazily decoded only when accessed (on-demand), (4) number parsing deferred to access time with SIMD-accelerated fast paths (Eisel-Lemire for floats, SWAR for integers), (5) total memory overhead is at most 8 bytes per JSON value (vs simdjson's ~16 bytes per tape entry). Correctness: parse and re-serialize all test files, verify byte-identical output.
